Listen to this article Share The Senate has called for an overhaul of security operations in Benue State following reported killings of 113 people in four separate attacks on communities in Katsina-Ala, Ukum and Logo Local Government Areas. The lawmakers urged the Federal Government, security agencies and the Benue State Government to take urgent and coordinated measures to stop the attacks, protect vulnerable communities and bring the perpetrators to justice. The Senate’s intervention followed a motion sponsored by Emmanuel Udende, representing Benue North-East Senatorial District, detailing the attacks and their impact on residents. The lawmakers expressed particular concern over the killing of six Mobile Police personnel in one of the incidents, raising questions about the ability of security agencies to protect civilians in the affected communities. Seconding the motion, Senator Jide Ipinsagba questioned the safety of residents in communities increasingly exposed to armed attacks. “If the security personnel are being killed, what happens to the civilians?” he asked. According to the motion, 24 people were reportedly killed in an attack on Sai community in Katsina-Ala Local Government Area, while another assault on Bom and Aboajio villages in Mbazun Council Ward, Ukum, claimed 63 lives. The two incidents accounted for 87 deaths and occurred during the Senate recess. Another attack on Ayilamo in Tombo Ward, Logo Local Government Area, reportedly left 15 people dead, including six Mobile Police personnel. Read also: NEC endorses 90-day action plan to ease cost of living for Nigerians The motion also recorded the killing of 11 people when attackers invaded Tse Biliji and Tse Shishi Nyako villages in Mbatian Council Ward, Ukum, on Thursday, October 8, 2026. The four incidents brought the reported death toll to 113. Udende warned that the recurring attacks had disrupted farming and other economic activities, destroyed livelihoods and heightened the risk of displacement. He urged the Federal Government, the state government and security agencies to act immediately to protect residents and restore peace in the affected areas. The senator also called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killings, stressing that the protection of lives and property remained a fundamental responsibility of government. Idayat Adebule also condemned the attacks and expressed condolences to the affected communities and the Nigeria Police Force. She called for intensified efforts to apprehend the perpetrators and provide humanitarian assistance to families whose homes and livelihoods had been destroyed. Adopting the motion, the Senate urged the Federal Government to take immediate steps to prevent further attacks in Ukum, Katsina-Ala, Logo and other vulnerable communities in Benue State. The lawmakers called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Chief of Army Staff and relevant security and intelligence chiefs to strengthen operations in the affected areas. They also demanded adequate deployment of security personnel, sufficient operational resources, improved intelligence gathering and early-warning systems to identify threats before attacks occur. The Senate further called for rapid-response mechanisms, thorough investigations into the killings and the prosecution of suspects found responsible. The lawmakers stressed the need for security agencies to prioritise preventive operations rather than respond only after communities had suffered casualties. Beyond security operations, the Senate expressed concern over the humanitarian consequences of the attacks, including the destruction of homes, loss of livelihoods and displacement of residents. It urged the National Emergency Management Agency to work with the Benue State Emergency Management Agency and other relevant authorities to provide immediate relief materials and assistance to victims. The Senate observed a minute of silence in honour of those killed and commiserated with the police over the reported deaths of six Mobile Police personnel. In his closing remarks, Senate President Godswill Akpabio directed the Senate Committee on Security and Intelligence to work with relevant agencies to examine the situation and identify measures to strengthen security operations and personnel deployment. The latest intervention adds to recurring calls by the National Assembly for stronger security measures in Benue State, where repeated attacks have resulted in deaths, displacement and disruption of farming activities. The Senate said coordinated security operations, reliable intelligence and rapid responses to emerging threats were necessary to prevent further killings and protect vulnerable communities.
